title: LangGraph persistence: checkpointers, stores, and thread IDs
request: According to the reviewed official LangGraph documentation, explain the scope of a checkpointer and a store, whether a thread_id is needed for thread persistence, and whether an in-memory checkpointer survives a process restart.

source.title: Persistence
source.license_note: This fixture paraphrases the public official documentation and keeps the source URL for review.

queries: LangGraph persistence checkpointer thread_id official docs
LangGraph store cross-thread memory official docs
LangGraph in-memory checkpointer restart official docs

documents.content: The persistence guide distinguishes checkpointers from stores. A checkpointer saves graph-state snapshots for one thread, while a store keeps application-defined data that can be shared across threads.
The documented quickstart compiles a graph with a checkpointer and invokes it with configurable.thread_id. The thread identifier groups checkpoints for the same thread.
The documentation states that an in-memory checkpointer keeps checkpoints in RAM and loses them when the process restarts. A persistent backend is needed when restart recovery is required.
